(Currently Amended) Claim 1: A system for generating a counter-stimulation in a patient suffering from RLS, the system comprising: a device configured and arranged to generate a counter-stimulation in a patient suffering from RLS, the counter-stimulation of an amplitude, intensity, and time duration either lower than that which would wake the patient and higher than that sufficient to relieve RLS symptoms, or sufficient to relieve RLS symptoms and allow the patient to return to sleep; a controller configured and arranged to drive the counter-stimulation generation device, the controller in communication with the counter-stimulation device; and a base configured and arranged to hold the counter-stimulation generation device adjacent to a patient, the counter-stimulation device attached to the base, wherein the device is selected from the group consisting of a vibration generator, a fluid pressure applicator, a mechanical point pressure applicator, a mechanical roller, a mechanical lift, a nerve stimulator, a muscle stimulator, a heater, a cooler, a chemical applicator, and a magnet.

(Currently Amended) Claim 2: The system according to Claim 1, wherein the device comprises a vibration generator selected from the group consisting of a piezo-chip, a loudspeaker, a motor with an eccentric weight, and a solenoid.

(Currently Amended) Claim 15: A method of treating RLS, the method comprising: selecting a patient experiencing RLS; stimulating a portion of the patient at an amplitude, intensity, and duration sufficient to act as a counter-stimulation to RLS and either to allow the patient to return to sleep or to not wake a sleeping patient, using one or more devices selected from the group consisting of vibration, pressure application, mechanical point pressure application, a mechanically rolling device against the patient's skin, mechanically lifting at least a portion of the patient, nerve stimulation, muscle stimulation, heat, cold, a chemical application, and magnetism.

(Currently Amended) Claim 18: The method according to Claim 15, wherein said counter-stimulation comprises mechanical vibration.
